== Unreleased changes (release date TBD)

https://github.com/oxidecomputer/progenitor/compare/v0.16.1\...HEAD[Full list of commits]

* Update typify to 0.10.1; types are generated by the typespace engine
  (typespace 0.1.2) and emitted through codespace 0.1.0 (#1433)
* Rework the `Generator` API (#1433)
** `Generator::build(&settings, &spec)` replaces `Generator::new`, `Default`,
   and `generate_tokens`; it processes the document once and returns any error
** `generate_sdk()`, `generate_cli(name)`, and `generate_httpmock(path)` replace
   `generate_tokens`, `cli(..)`, and `httpmock(..)`; each returns a
   `codespace::Codespace` (`.into_stream()` gives the `TokenStream`)
** `typespace()` replaces `get_type_space`; `uses_futures` and `uses_websockets`
   are gone (the codespace's dependencies say what the code needs)
* Replace `GenerationSettings::with_derive` and `with_map_type` with
  `map_typespace_settings` (#1433)
* Return `Error::UnsupportedSettings` from `Generator::build` for the positional
  interface with separate tags, rather than panicking (#1433)
* Track the crates generated code needs through the codespace: `generate_sdk`,
  `generate_cli`, and `generate_httpmock` register every crate their code names,
  with the versions and features progenitor is tested against, and
  cargo-progenitor writes the generated crate's `[dependencies]` from that (now
  base64 0.23, rand 0.10, regress 0.12, and progenitor-client at the matching
  version) (#1436)
* Add `--json-body-schema` to generated CLIs and remove the
  `--json-body-template` stub; the generated `CliConfig` trait has a new
  required method, `json_body_schema` (#1441)
* Emit the SDK's `builder` as a codespace module (so file output gives it its
  own file) and move `prelude` to the top of the generated code (#1443)
* Changes to generated types that come from typespace (#1433)
** Integer newtypes no longer implement `TryFrom<&str>` or `TryFrom<String>`;
   `FromStr` remains
** `types::error::ConversionError` is omitted when nothing uses it
** Patterns compile in Unicode mode (the `u` flag), so a pattern that is valid
   only without it fails `Generator::build`
** `JsonSchema` impls use `schemars::r#gen`, so they compile in edition 2024
   crates
* Treat `derives` in `generate_api!` as typespace trait names, parsed by
  `TraitSpec`: a trait typespace models (such as `Hash` or
  `schemars::JsonSchema`) is required of every generated type, any other path is
  emitted as a derive, and a bad name is an error at that derive (#1433)
* Deprecate the `pre_hook`, `pre_hook_async`, `post_hook`, and
  `post_hook_async` settings (and the matching `GenerationSettings::with_*`
  methods) in favor of `ClientHooks` (#1457)
* Fix a panic in builder-style generation for object-type query parameters
  (#1456)
* Read the OpenAPI document in one call in `progenitor-macro` (#1454)
* Raise the MSRV to 1.97 (#1433)

=== Migrating from 0.16

If you only use `generate_api!`, the thing to check is `derives`. A trait
typespace models is now required of every generated type, so generation fails
if one can't implement it.

A `build.rs` written for 0.16 created a `Generator` and then handed it the
document:

[source,rust]
----
let mut generator = progenitor::Generator::default();
let tokens = generator.generate_tokens(&spec).unwrap();
----

In 0.17 the generator is built from the settings and the document together,
and generation itself can't fail:

[source,rust]
----
let generator = progenitor::Generator::build(
    &progenitor::GenerationSettings::default(),
    &spec,
)
.unwrap();
let tokens = generator.generate_sdk().into_stream();
----

`generate_cli` and `generate_httpmock` work the same way. If you want to know
which crates the generated code needs, ask the `Codespace` (`dependencies()`)
before `into_stream()` consumes it.

`with_derive` and `with_map_type` become `map_typespace_settings`, which hands
you the typespace settings to adjust:

[source,rust]
----
use progenitor::typespace::TypespaceTrait;
use progenitor::typespace::settings::{ContainerType, ForeignTrait};

let mut settings = progenitor::GenerationSettings::default();
settings.map_typespace_settings(|s| {
    // was: settings.with_derive("schemars::JsonSchema")
    s.with_required_trait(TypespaceTrait::JsonSchema)
        // was: settings.with_derive("my_crate::MyDerive")
        .with_derive(ForeignTrait::new("::my_crate::MyDerive").unwrap())
        // was: settings.with_map_type("std::collections::BTreeMap")
        .with_map_type(ContainerType::btree_map())
});
----

Generated CLIs have a `--json-body-schema` flag, so a `CliConfig` impl needs
one more method:

[source,rust]
----
fn json_body_schema<T>(&self)
where
    T: schemars::JsonSchema + serde::Serialize + std::fmt::Debug,
{
    let schema = schemars::schema_for!(T);
    println!("{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&schema).unwrap());
}
----

=== Migrating from the hook settings

The body of a pre hook moves into `ClientHooks::pre` and the body of a post
hook into `ClientHooks::post`, implemented for the generated `Client`. Both
methods are async and take the same request or response the hook did, plus an
`&OperationInfo`. The inner type is the trait's type parameter, reached through
`self.inner()`. A hook that returned `Result<_, E>` maps its error to
`Error::Custom(e.to_string())`, which is what the generated code did for it.

[source,rust]
----
impl ClientHooks<Inner> for Client {
    async fn pre<E>(
        &self,
        req: &mut reqwest::Request,
        _info: &OperationInfo,
    ) -> Result<(), Error<E>> {
        // the former pre_hook body, with `inner` as `self.inner()`
        Ok(())
    }
}
----
